# Multi-Tenant Document Store REST API Design

## Resource Hierarchy

```
GET    /organizations/{org_id}
GET    /organizations/{org_id}/documents
POST   /organizations/{org_id}/documents
GET    /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}
PUT    /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}
DELETE /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}

GET    /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}/versions
GET    /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}/versions/{version_id}
POST   /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}/restore
```

**Why:** Org ID in path enforces tenant isolation at routing layer. Documents nested under org. Versions as sub-resource (not top-level) makes dependency explicit.

---

## Authentication & Authorization

**Bearer Token (JWT)**
```
Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token>
```

Token payload:
```json
{
  "sub": "user_id",
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "roles": ["editor", "viewer"],
  "exp": 1234567890
}
```

**Scopes:** `documents:read`, `documents:write`, `documents:admin`

**Why:** JWT stateless (no session store). Org ID in token prevents cross-tenant token reuse. Roles allow fine-grained access; middleware checks both token org + route org match.

---

## Authorization Rules

```
- Viewer: GET documents only
- Editor: GET, POST, PUT (own org)
- Admin: DELETE, restore, org settings
- Org isolation: token.org_id must == route.org_id (enforced in middleware)
```

---

## Pagination

```
GET /organizations/{org_id}/documents?page=2&limit=25&sort=-created_at

Response:
{
  "data": [...],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 2,
    "limit": 25,
    "total": 487,
    "has_next": true,
    "has_prev": true
  }
}
```

**Why:** Cursor-less (simpler), limit+page (common). Metadata separate from data. Always include `total` for UI (progress bars). Sort via query param (handles `-created_at` desc syntax).

**Alternative considered:** Cursor-based. Better for large datasets + consistency under concurrent deletes. Skip if scale is <1M docs per tenant.

---

## Versioning Strategy

**Automatic on every PUT (immutable versions)**

```
PUT /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}
{
  "title": "New title",
  "content": "..."
}

Response 200:
{
  "id": "doc_123",
  "version": 5,
  "title": "New title",
  "created_at": "2026-11-06T10:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-06T10:05:00Z"
}
```

**List versions:**
```
GET /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}/versions?limit=10

{
  "data": [
    {
      "version": 5,
      "title": "New title",
      "updated_at": "2026-11-06T10:05:00Z",
      "updated_by": "user_456"
    },
    {
      "version": 4,
      "title": "Old title",
      "updated_at": "2026-11-06T10:00:00Z",
      "updated_by": "user_123"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {...}
}
```

**Restore version:**
```
POST /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}/restore
{
  "version": 4
}

Response 201:
{
  "id": "doc_123",
  "version": 6,
  "title": "Old title (restored from v4)",
  "restored_from": 4
}
```

**Why:** Auto-versioning → no accidental data loss. Restore creates new version (audit trail, not destructive). Version number (not timestamp) avoids clock skew issues. Metadata (updated_by) enables accountability.

---

## Error Format

**Consistent error response:**
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "Document title cannot be empty",
    "details": {
      "field": "title",
      "constraint": "min_length=1"
    },
    "request_id": "req_abc123xyz",
    "timestamp": "2026-11-06T10:05:23Z"
  }
}
```

**HTTP Status + Code mapping:**

| Status | Code | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` | Malformed input |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | Missing/invalid token |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Token valid, but no permission |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Document/org not found |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | Version mismatch (concurrent edit) |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Input fails schema |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Too many requests |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Server error |

**Why:** Single error object (vs nested). `code` machine-readable (client retries/handling). `details` for form validation. `request_id` links to logs. Timestamp aids debugging.

---

## Concurrent Edit Protection

```
PUT /organizations/{org_id}/documents/{doc_id}
{
  "title": "Updated",
  "if_version": 4  // Optimistic lock
}

Conflict scenario (version advanced to 5):
Response 409:
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VERSION_CONFLICT",
    "message": "Document was updated by another user",
    "details": {
      "current_version": 5,
      "expected_version": 4
    }
  }
}
```

**Why:** Prevents lost updates. Client fetches current version, sends back in PUT. Server rejects if mismatch. Simpler than locks, fits REST semantics.

---

## Key Design Decisions Summary

| Decision | Benefit | Tradeoff |
|----------|---------|----------|
| **Org in path** | Tenant isolation enforced early | Path longer, less flexible multi-org queries |
| **Automatic versioning** | Zero data loss, audit trail | Storage overhead (~10-20% with compression) |
| **JWT in token body** | Stateless, org ID verified client-side | Cannot revoke instantly (TTL mitigates) |
| **Limit+page pagination** | Simple, familiar | Not consistent under deletes (cursor better for immutable feeds) |
| **Optimistic locking** | No locks held, scales horizontally | Client must handle 409 retries |
| **Separate error object** | Extensible, one schema | Extra nesting |

---

## Example Flows

**Create document:**
```
POST /organizations/org_123/documents
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
{
  "title": "Q4 Report",
  "content": "...",
  "tags": ["finance", "2026"]
}

201 Created
{
  "id": "doc_456",
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "version": 1,
  "title": "Q4 Report",
  "created_at": "2026-11-06T10:05:00Z",
  "created_by": "user_123"
}
```

**Edit with conflict:**
```
PUT /organizations/org_123/documents/doc_456
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
{
  "title": "Q4 Report (Final)",
  "if_version": 1
}

409 Conflict (another editor already bumped to v2)
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VERSION_CONFLICT",
    "current_version": 2,
    "expected_version": 1
  }
}

Client must GET, merge changes, retry with version 2
```

---

**Setup:** Use middleware to enforce `token.org_id == route.org_id` before controller runs. This prevents token reuse across tenants even if bug in business logic.
